title: Ensembling LLM-Induced Decision Trees for Explainable and Robust Error Detection

problem.claim: Error detection identifies incorrect or inconsistent cell values in tabular data to support data quality.

gap.claim: LLM-as-a-labeler methods lack traceable justifications and robustness because they use implicit black-box, single-pass inference susceptible to stochasticity.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes TreeED, an LLM-as-an-inducer framework that induces decision trees for error detection.
TreeED combines rule nodes, GNN nodes, and leaf nodes to represent validation checks, complex patterns, and final error or clean decisions.

The paper proposes ForestED, which ensembles trees built from informative row subsets and uses an Expectation-Maximization-based algorithm to estimate tree reliability and optimize consensus predictions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report that the methods are accurate, explainable, and robust.
The methods reportedly improve average F1-score by 16.1% over the best baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Error detection is important for maintaining tabular data quality, and recent methods use LLMs to label erroneous cells.
LLM-as-a-labeler pipelines provide little explicit justification and produce inconsistent detections under single-pass stochastic inference.

TreeED induces decision-tree skeletons whose root-to-leaf paths specify stepwise sample evaluation, while ForestED constructs multiple trees from informative subsets and optimizes consensus predictions.
Experiments report accuracy, explainability, robustness, and a 16.1% average F1-score improvement over the best baseline.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baseline identities, or experimental settings.
